presentation.label: IMPROVED AMP
presentation.summary: The AMP page reworked: HLD from no hold to AUTO, shown in steps; ATK, DEC and REL in fine steps from 0.2 ms, shown as times; a finer OVR; and ENV RESET AMP without a click.
presentation.overview: Improved AMP reworks the AMP page. HLD runs from 0 (no hold: the decay starts the moment the attack reaches the top) up to AUTO at the top of the knob (hold while the note lasts), never cuts the attack short, and reads in steps at the current tempo and track speed. AMP ATK and DEC and FILTER ATK, DEC and REL step 0.2 ms at a time up to 5 ms, stay finer than stock up to 300 ms and show times instead of 0..127. OVR keeps its range but spreads the overdrive evenly over the knob, so the low end is fine. SOUND SETTINGS > ENV RESET gains AMP and AMP+FILT: the amp envelope restarts from silence on every sequenced trig and retrig, without a click, so AMP ATK is heard on every hit. The module is always on.
highlights: HLD: 0 = no hold, top = AUTO, shown in steps; never cuts the attack.
ATK, DEC and REL: 0.2 ms steps at the low end, shown in ms and s.
OVR: a fine low end, the same range.
ENV RESET AMP and AMP+FILT: every sequenced trig starts from silence, without a click.
usage: Press AMP. Turn DEC down: the knob shows its time to -60 dB, in 0.2 ms steps below 5 ms.
Turn HLD to 0: the decay starts as soon as the attack peaks. Turn it up: the knob shows the hold in steps at the current tempo (1.00 is one step). At the top it reads AUTO (decay from note-off).
Hold FUNC and turn HLD: it jumps between 0, 124.7 ms (one step at 120 BPM) and AUTO.
Turn OVR up from 0: the first values add drive gently.
On an analog BD sound set ATK to about 40 and DEC to 100 or more, and place trigs on every second step. Press PLAY: the attack is heard on the first trig only.
Open the SOUND menu (FUNC + MUTE) > SOUND SETTINGS and set ENV RESET to AMP: every trig now fades in at the ATK rate, without a click.

access.location: AMP page (ATK, HLD, DEC, OVR); FILTER page (ATK, DEC, REL); SOUND menu (FUNC + MUTE) > SOUND SETTINGS > ENV RESET.
steps: Turn HLD, ATK, DEC or OVR; FUNC + turn on HLD jumps between 0, 124.7 ms and AUTO.
For ENV RESET AMP: FUNC + MUTE > SOUND SETTINGS > ENV RESET, then LEFT or RIGHT to AMP or AMP+FILT.

controls.name: AMP > HLD
controls.doc: 0 no hold, then 0.67 ms steps to 10 ms, 1.3 ms to 18 ms, 3.3 ms to 51 ms, 6.7 ms to 151 ms, 13 ms to 298 ms, about 6 % a step to 15.5 s, AUTO at the top. The number is the hold in steps of the selected track at the current tempo and speed (1.00 = one step). The decay never starts before the attack peaks.

controls.name: AMP > ATK
controls.doc: 0 instant, 0.2 ms steps to 5 ms, 0.5 ms steps to 15 ms, then about 10 % a step to 30 s.

controls.name: FILTER > ATK
controls.doc: The same curve as AMP ATK: 0 instant, 0.2 ms steps to 5 ms, 0.5 ms steps to 15 ms, then about 10 % a step to 30 s.

controls.name: AMP > DEC, FILTER > DEC and REL
controls.doc: 0 instant, 0.2 ms steps to 5 ms, 0.5 ms to 15 ms, 1 ms to 25 ms, 2.5 ms to 50 ms, 5 ms to 100 ms, 10 ms to 200 ms, 25 ms to 300 ms, then about 14 % a step to 40-45 s. Times are to -60 dB. AMP DEC at the top stays INF.

controls.name: AMP > OVR
controls.doc: The stock range, 0 and 127 as stock, with the overdrive's rise spread evenly over the knob: stock's first step takes about eight values. The number stays 0..127.

controls.name: SOUND SETTINGS > ENV RESET
controls.doc: Steps OFF, AMP, FILTER, AMP+FILT. With AMP in the value, the amp envelope restarts from silence on every sequenced trig and retrig of this sound; the voice fades out just before the trig.

limitations: Built for OS 1.74 only, on Modwerk's Rytm base with the amp record hook (ev_amp_record).

Always on: saved HLD, ATK, DEC, REL and OVR values read differently from stock while it is installed. HLD 0 is no hold instead of AUTO, 127 is AUTO instead of 16 s, and the others follow the new curves. Removing the module plays every project as before.
Cannot be installed with Env Reset Amp: this module carries ENV RESET's AMP and AMP+FILT itself.
ENV RESET AMP acts on trigs the Rytm schedules itself: pad hits, MIDI notes and the first trig after PLAY play as stock.
With AMP set, a sounding voice is silent for up to about 7 ms before each sequenced trig; a retrig roll faster than twice that gets half its spacing to sound.
A retrig hit that lands less than 7 ms before the track's next trig starts and is faded out again at once.
On external MIDI clock a tick that arrives late shortens the next fade by as much; after a tick 6 ms or more late, the next trig plays as stock.
HLD's number counts steps at the tempo when it is drawn; the hold itself is a fixed time and does not follow tempo.

Times shown are calibrated to one Rytm MKII (AMP attack 0.957x, decay 0.918x; the filter envelope runs at the OS model's speed), and OVR's curve to that unit's overdrive; another unit may differ slightly.
On stock firmware a sound saved here plays the stock way, with ENV RESET's amp bit ignored.

claims: ui:value text of AMP ATK/HLD/DEC and FILTER ATK/DEC/REL

load.display: Small: a short C call per voice while its amp envelope moves, and a 12-track scan a block with ENV RESET AMP in use
load.conditions: Read in the code: the amp record write skips a voice whose record repeats and changed nothing, so an idle voice makes no C call; with no AMP in any track's ENV RESET the pre-fade reads the 12 ENV RESET bytes once a block and skips its scan; the OVR reader adds one table lookup a voice a block. On the author's MKII an earlier build of the envelope code in a 16-module set (LR03, private telemetry base, sequencer stopped) read 70.37 % of the audio block idle, against 70.84 % before that skip (LR01); the module's own share was not separated, and this version's build was not measured.

hardware.summary: Run hands off by npp1993's (the author's) automated USB test rig on their Analog Rytm MKII, OS 1.74, on 9 and 10 November 2026, as the rig's run record reports: image IL02 (sha256 a569c9f5), this source alone on a development build of the Modwerk base with a USB test link, loaded to RAM. 25 cases passed. Screens: ATK, DEC and FILTER times, HLD in steps at 90, 120 and 139 BPM and three track speeds, FUNC + turn on HLD, ENV RESET's four values, a kit save and reload. Sound on the BD voice over USB audio: lengths by DEC, HLD and AUTO; OVR's level curve and the FILTER times beside the same base without the module; ENV RESET AMP's fade before sequenced trigs, retrigs, swung and micro-timed trigs and sound-locked trigs, and none for MIDI notes, the first trig after PLAY, muted trigs, lock trigs and trigs whose condition fails.
limitations: Run by an automated rig, not by hand or by ear; pads were not played.
Loaded to RAM beside a development USB test link: this package's own image (IA08) and a boot from flash were not run.
No power cycle, project save and load, Sound pool or +Drive sound, external MIDI clock, pattern change or probability condition.
The first note after loading an image to RAM was near silent in some boots, also on the image without the module (1 of 7 boots; 10 of 18 with it); cause not found.
Memory and audio load were not measured on the unit. Duration not recorded.

tests.summary: On the author's Analog Rytm MKII (OS 1.74), run by their automated USB test rig on 9 and 10 November 2026, as reported: 25 cases pass on IL02, this source on a development base with a USB test link, loaded to RAM: the AMP and FILTER screens, HLD in steps, lengths by DEC and HLD, OVR's curve and the FILTER times beside stock's, and ENV RESET AMP's fade across sequenced trigs, retrigs, swing, micro timing, sound locks, mutes and trig conditions. rytm-emu runs of this package's own build (IA08). Not run: pads, a power cycle, a boot from flash, an external clock. See TESTING.md.
